images.caption: Figure 1:Cross-modal redistribution.A large fraction of visual tokens in an Omni-LLM are redundant. Our method projects audio and video into a common space to drop redundant visual tokens, then replaces the discarded object semantics with compact text proxies, redistributing visual information across the audio and text streams.

Figure 3:Audio and visual embeddings on VGGSound test set.Left:raw space by PCA, where the two modalities separate and differ
in spread.Right:our projection along the top two canonical components. The
paired embeddings now overlap in a common space, making audio-visual similarity
directly measurable.

Figure 4:Hyperparameter sensitivity of ReMo, measured on World. with the 3B backbone. We vary the selection budgetρa​v\rho_{av}, local detail budgetρl\rho_{l}, temporal merging thresholdτ\tau, and number of canonical directionsKKindividually. Red curves show accuracy and blue curves the compression rate, except retrieval R@1 forKK. Dashed lines mark the default setting. Accuracy remains stable, showing ReMo is robust to these choices.

Figure E.1:Attention on the injected text proxiesacross decoder layers on
the 3B model. In mean attention, both within-chunk and text-prompt queries
attend more to the injected text than to the video tokens across most layers.
The maximum attention varies by layer, but the consistently higher mean indicates
that the proxies are broadly attended, not reached only by a few outlier heads.

Figure J.1:Text proxies supporting question answering after pruning.Three examples compare the full-token model, OmniSelect, and ReMo. ReMo retains the correct answers while exposing object identities through spatially grounded proxies. Black patches indicate pruned visual tokens, and orange labels show text proxies at their TMRoPE positions. By providing object identities and locations, the proxies help the model focus on temporal, spatial, and causal relations in the retained evidence.

Figure J.2:Failure cases of semantic offloading.ReMo answers incorrectly where the full-token model succeeds. From top to bottom, the examples illustrate emphasis on a distracting attribute, incorrect detector labels, and a missed-detection error in which YOLO detects only one of three vehicles. Black patches indicate pruned visual tokens, orange labels denote text proxies, and red outlines highlight misleading proxies. The examples show how distracting labels and detector errors can mislead downstream reasoning.

Figure J.3:Common space alignment for visual pruning and audio-to-video retrieval.Top: compared with the raw space, projection prunes additional tokens around sound sources. Yellow dashed boxes mark sound sources, red outlines mark tokens dropped only in the common space, and black patches indicate pruned tokens. Bottom: the paired videos for snare-drum and table-tennis audio move from ranks 46 and 89 to rank 1; green borders mark the retrieved paired videos.
